judge_reasoning: The ImageNet CVPR 2009 paper by Deng et al. with DOI 10.1109/CVPR.2009.5206848 is a well-known real work. The author 'Sorokin' is a garbled substitution for 'Socher' (the §6 taxonomy explicitly cites this exact example as REAL-with-metadata-error); title, year, venue, DOI, and first-author surname all uniquely identify the real paper.
The citation exactly matches the canonical Transformer paper: Vaswani et al., 'Attention Is All You Need,' NeurIPS 2017, arXiv:1706.03762, with the correct coauthor list and page range.

Warren & Marshall published 'Unidentified Curved Bacilli on Gastric Epithelium in Active Chronic Gastritis' in The Lancet 1983 (321:1273-1275). The cited title is a paraphrase but authors, year, and venue uniquely identify this real work.
The BERT paper by Devlin, Chang, Lee, Toutanova (arXiv:1810.04805, NAACL-HLT 2019) is confirmed on arXiv and ACL Anthology with exact title, authors, year, and venue match.

Mata v. Avianca, Inc. is a well-documented S.D.N.Y. 2023 case (678 F.Supp.3d 443) in which Judge Castel sanctioned attorneys for submitting ChatGPT-fabricated citations. Title, venue, and year match exactly.

No U.S.-based post-exposure prophylaxis trial named 'RECOVER' exists for hydroxychloroquine/COVID-19. The major U.S. HCQ PEP trial included in Cochrane reviews is Boulware et al. (NEJM 2020), not 'RECOVER.' The UK RECOVERY trial studied HCQ as treatment (not PEP), and the NIH RECOVER initiative studies long COVID. The cited trial does not match any real work.

Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436 (1966) is a landmark U.S. Supreme Court case verified by Justia, Library of Congress, GovInfo, and FindLaw. The case name, reporter citation (volume 384, page 436), and year all match official records.
PubMed (PMID 8298418) confirms the exact title, author 'Antiplatelet Trialists' Collaboration', year 1994, venue BMJ, volume 308(6921), pages 81-106. This is a well-known landmark meta-analysis.

Obergefell v. Hodges, 576 U.S. 644 (2015), is a landmark Supreme Court decision on same-sex marriage rights, decided June 26, 2015. Case name, venue (SCOTUS), and year all match the cited attribution exactly.

The Antiplatelet Trialists' Collaboration published a landmark multi-part meta-analysis in BMJ in 1994 (vol 308), including 'Collaborative overview of randomised trials of antiplatelet therapy--I: Prevention of death, myocardial infarction, and stroke...' (PMID 8298418). Title, venue, year, and corporate author all match.
Exact title match for Marshall & Warren's landmark 1984 Lancet paper (vol 323, pp 1311-1315). Authors, year, and venue all match.
Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436 (1966) confirmed by Justia, Library of Congress, GovInfo, FindLaw. Case caption, reporter (vol 384, page 436), year, and venue all match.
ImageNet CVPR 2009 by Deng, Dong, Socher, Li, Li, Fei-Fei exists with the exact title, venue, pages 248-255, and DOI. Cited byline garbles 'Socher' as 'Sorolina' — metadata error per §6.
DOI 10.18653/v1/N19-1423 resolves to the cited work: Devlin, Chang, Lee, Toutanova (2019) BERT NAACL-HLT 2019, pp 4171-4186. All fields match.
Mata v. Avianca, Inc., 678 F.Supp.3d 443 (S.D.N.Y. 2023). Real, well-documented federal case in which Judge Castel sanctioned attorneys for ChatGPT-fabricated brief.
Title, authors (Devlin, Chang, Lee, Toutanova), year (2019), venue (NAACL 2019) all match ACL Anthology N19-1423.
Loving v. Virginia, 388 U.S. 1 (1967) confirmed by Justia, Library of Congress U.S. Reports, and Wikipedia at the exact citation given.
Marshall & Warren 1984 Lancet 'Unidentified curved bacilli in the stomach of patients with gastritis and peptic ulceration' confirmed at pages 1311-1315. Title, authors, year, venue all match.

Cochrane Review on HCQ for COVID-19 prevention/treatment was authored by Singh B et al. 2021 (CD013587.pub2), not Fiolet. Fiolet et al. 2021 is a real but different paper in Clinical Microbiology and Infection. The byline points to a different real work than the title/venue indicates — EXISTENT_WRONG_ID.
Title, first-author surname (Devlin), year (2019), venue (NAACL 2019), arXiv ID (1810.04805) all match canonical BERT paper.
Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436 (1966) is a well-known landmark U.S. Supreme Court decision. Case name, reporter citation, and year all canonically correct.
DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD013587 resolves to the real Cochrane review by Singh, Ryan, Kredo, Chaplin, Fletcher (2021), not Axfors et al. Axfors is a real author of a different work. EXISTENT_WRONG_ID.
Title, author group (ISIS-2 Collaborative Group), year (1988), venue (Lancet), and DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(88)92833-4 all match canonical Lancet publication (PMID 2903874).
Canonical Vaswani et al. 2017 'Attention is all you need' NeurIPS 2017, arXiv:1706.03762. All fields match.
Loving v. Virginia, 388 U.S. 1 (1967), decided June 12, 1967. Confirmed by Justia, LOC, Oyez, Wikipedia.
Loving v. Virginia, 388 U.S. 1 (1967) landmark unanimous SCOTUS decision striking down anti-miscegenation laws. Citation, reporter, year all match.
Exact match: Deng, Dong, Socher, Li, Li, Fei-Fei (2009) ImageNet at 2009 IEEE CVPR. Widely cited foundational paper.
Vaswani et al. 'Attention Is All You Need' (2017) NeurIPS, arXiv:1706.03762. All fields match.
Loving v. Virginia, 388 U.S. 1 (1967) is a landmark US Supreme Court case widely documented. Caption, reporter, year all correct.
Vaswani et al., 'Attention Is All You Need,' NeurIPS 2017, arXiv:1706.03762 - canonical Transformer paper. All fields match.
Marshall & Warren (1984), 'Unidentified curved bacilli in the stomach of patients with gastritis and peptic ulceration,' The Lancet 323:1311-1315. Canonical H. pylori paper.
Cassell & Fowles (1998), 'Handcuffing the Cops?', 50 Stanford Law Review 1055. Title, authors, year, venue, volume, starting page all match SSRN and published PDF.
ISIS-2 Collaborative Group RCT of streptokinase and aspirin among 17,187 acute MI patients in The Lancet 1988. Trial name, year, venue, 17,187/417-hospital details all match.
Marshall & Warren 1984 Lancet paper confirmed with exact title, authors, venue, pages 1311-1315, issue 8390. Landmark H. pylori discovery paper.
WOSCOPS (West of Scotland Coronary Prevention Study) is a real landmark RCT of pravastatin published in NEJM 1995, widely cited in cardiology literature.

Title, year (1983), venue (Lancet), issue (8336), and pages (1273-1275) uniquely identify the real Warren & Marshall paper. Cited byline lists Marshall as sole author when paper is Warren & Marshall (Warren first) - but per §6 this is a metadata error on an otherwise unambiguous match, so REAL.
Rachel F. Moran's 'Interracial Intimacy: The Regulation of Race and Romance,' University of Chicago Press 2001. Title, author, year, venue all match publisher's own page.
Canonical Vaswani et al. 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' NeurIPS 2017, arXiv:1706.03762. All fields match.
ISIS-2 published in The Lancet 1988, enrolling 17,187 patients with suspected acute MI, establishing aspirin's efficacy. Title, venue, year, enrollment number all match.
Mata v. Avianca, Inc. S.D.N.Y. 2023 sanctions opinion (2023 WL 4015181, Judge Castel). Title, venue, court, judge, year all match.

No record exists of Schulhofer article 'The practice of law as confidence game: Charlene Wear Simmons gets it right' in Michigan Law Review 94(6) 1935-1948 or anywhere. Schulhofer's known 1996 Miranda piece was in Northwestern University Law Review; 'confidence game' framing belongs to Richard Leo's 1996 Law & Society Review article. Cited title is a fabricated mashup.
Braunwald's Heart Disease: A Textbook of Cardiovascular Medicine is a widely cited cardiology reference textbook by/edited by Eugene Braunwald. Title and author surname match.
ISIS-2 is a real landmark trial published in The Lancet on 13 August 1988 by the ISIS-2 Collaborative Group. Title, year, short-name all match.

Axfors & Ioannidis 2021 published an international meta-analysis of randomized trials of HCQ/chloroquine in COVID-19 (Nature Communications 12:2349), not Epidemiology. Per §6 the venue transcription error on an otherwise-identifiable real work (correct first author, senior author, year, topic) is REAL-with-metadata-error.
4S (Scandinavian Simvastatin Survival Study) is a real landmark RCT of simvastatin in 4,444 CHD patients, published in The Lancet in 1994. Trial name and venue match.
BERT by Devlin, Chang, Lee, Toutanova posted to arXiv as 1810.04805 in October 2018. Title, authors, year, arXiv ID all match canonical record; 10.48550/arXiv.<id> is arXiv's standard DOI format.

Phyl Newbeck did publish a 2004 book 'Virginia Hasn't Always Been for Lovers' about the Loving case. Main title + author + year uniquely identify the work. Cited subtitle (Interracial marriages and the resistance to assimilation...) and publisher (University of Chicago Press) are wrong (actual: 'Interracial Marriage Bans and the Case of Richard and Mildred Loving' / Southern Illinois University Press) but per §6 these are metadata errors on an otherwise identifiable real work.
Title, first-author surname (Russakovsky), year (2015), venue (IJCV), volume/pages (115, 211-252), and DOI all match Springer Nature record.
Exact match on title, all six authors (Deng, Dong, Socher, Li, Li, Fei-Fei), year 2009, venue (CVPR 2009), pages 248-255 confirmed via Semantic Scholar and Princeton publications.
Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436 (1966) is a landmark U.S. Supreme Court decision confirmed by U.S. Reports on loc.gov, Justia, FindLaw, GovInfo. Reporter citation, year, and venue all match.
